basis: Dextrocardia defines cardiac malposition; mirror-image abdominal organs generally function normally. Associated cardiac defects and ciliary disease are not universal.
Congenital fusion of proximal finger joints with associated skeletal abnormalities.
Defining skin fragility, interstitial lung disease and nephrotic renal disease; skin blistering and nephrotic syndrome each documented in 3/3 patients.
Lysosomal storage disorder with progressive neurodegeneration; damaging retinal disease is common, including rod-cone dystrophy in 5/5 patients.
Mosaic schwannomatosis produces schwannomas arising from peripheral nerve sheaths; other organ involvement is not established across this concept.
Corneal dyskeratosis, palmoplantar hyperkeratosis and laryngeal dyskeratosis define the syndrome; the larynx belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Oral/GI injury ~80-100%, contractures 80-99%, ocular involvement 30-79%; these fill the cap. Anemia is secondary; renal and cardiac damage occur in <30%.
Posterior displacement of the ocular lens.
Benign fibroblastic neoplasm arising from the cranium with osteolytic bone destruction.
Osteochondrodysplasia directly affects cartilage, growth plates and bones; proposed nutritional contributors do not establish a metabolic disorder.
Disordered neuronal migration produces heterotopic brain tissue; seizures and migration abnormalities occur in 80-99%.
Disease of peripheral nerve plexuses; no additional organ damage applies across this umbrella.
Immune-mediated inflammatory chorioretinal disease; cerebral vasculitis and permanent neurological complications are uncommon (<30%).
Malignant neoplasm originating in the epiglottis, part of the upper airway.
Loss of central recognition of familiar voices is an auditory agnosia, rather than peripheral hearing loss.
Cavitating cerebral leukodystrophy; optic atrophy is reported in 30-79%, and ovarian endocrine failure is frequent in affected females. Renal abnormalities occur in <30%.
Pancreatic carcinoma with both malignant ductal and endocrine components, involving exocrine and endocrine pancreatic tissue.
Inherited coagulation disorder defined by abnormal bleeding and prolonged bleeding time.
Primary magnesium transport disorder with renal tubular magnesium wasting and defining intellectual disability.
Congenital failure of femoral bone continuity and union, producing a false joint.
Immune-mediated inflammatory bowel disease; extraintestinal damage is not established as common for this subtype.
Carcinoma originates in the stomach; neuroendocrine differentiation does not establish disease of an endocrine gland.
Mesothelial tumour originating in the pleura.
Facial skeletal overgrowth and strabismus/amblyopia define the syndrome. Cleft palate occurs in <30%; hair distribution changes do not establish skin damage.
Inherited immune dysregulation predisposes to SPTCL and HLH; skin infiltration and hematologic injury belong to those separately diagnosed diseases, not susceptibility alone.
